findings.title: Docs claim any throw from source read releases it, but serializer errors don't
findings.claim: The documentation states that any exception thrown while reading from a source releases it, but process_one_buffer calls unmarshall outside any handler, so an exception there leaves _source_closed false and stream_close() never runs; only stream_receive() failures and eof actually release the source, so an application following the doc literally will leak the connection.

findings.title: Queue-drain half of the fix has no test coverage
findings.claim: The new test has the outgoing queue empty by construction when stream_close() runs, so deleting the std::exchange(_outgoing_queue_ready, ...) wait would not fail any existing test; it is coverable using suspend_for_testing() to park the queue and assert close_entered stays false, which also covers the untested 'sink closed first, source eof last' ordering.

findings.title: Test never asserts that the frame send was actually refused
findings.claim: The catch (const rpc::closed_error&) swallows the expected outcome, and a successful hook call would also pass the test; detection relies entirely on put_after_close, which needs the batch flush poller to run before the check. Should use BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW to directly assert the closed_error.

findings.title: yield() loop does not guarantee the flush poller actually runs
findings.claim: yield() only schedules an empty task; pollers run when the queue drains or quota expires, so without the fix the test could fail either on put_after_close or on the ~output_stream assert depending on timing, making the accompanying comment inaccurate. check_for_io_immediately() would force a poll, and the loop becomes unnecessary if refusal is asserted directly.

findings.title: Comment misstates why _outgoing_queue_ready becomes exceptional
findings.claim: The comment says _outgoing_queue_ready is exceptional if an entry failed, but a failed send_entry calls abort() and still runs p->done.set_value(), so a failed entry never makes the chain exceptional; the actual causes are stop_send_loop() withdrawing queued entries and the _negotiated abort.

findings.title: Comment 'nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from here on' is inaccurate
findings.claim: stop_send_loop() still does when_all on _outgoing_queue_ready (it just receives the ready placeholder); also the retained comment at rpc.cc:563-564 now sits far from the _sink_closed_future = p.get_future() line it explains and should be moved.

findings.title: Stale plain-// comment lines break the new doxygen blocks
findings.claim: The old '// send data Out...' and '// receive data In...' lines now sit between the new /// doxygen block and the declaration, and the rest of the file uses a plain first line rather than \brief for consistency; these stale lines should be removed.

findings.title: Doc overstates that the stream connection is shut down 'only' when both halves close
findings.claim: The connection can also be shut down by a read-loop failure or by closing the parent client via abort_all_streams(), which the doc itself acknowledges earlier, so the word 'only' is too strong.

findings.title: const_cast used in hook-capturing factory instead of a mutable member
findings.claim: Declaring hooks as mutable would be cleaner than casting away const on this.

findings.title: PR body and commits carry Claude attribution trailers, violating user's global rule
findings.claim: The PR body ends with a 'Generated with Claude Code' line and all three commits carry Co-Authored-By: Claude trailers, which violates the user's global CLAUDE.md instruction to never add these; they should be stripped before merge.
